title: Carpet vs Hardwood for Resale Value in Edmonds
meta: For resale in Edmonds, hardwood wins the main floor and fresh carpet still wins bedrooms and stairs. Wills Flooring explains what buyers reward, room by room.
keywords: carpet vs hardwood resale value, does carpet hurt resale value, new carpet before selling house, hardwood or carpet in bedrooms for resale, flooring for selling a house Edmonds WA

blocks.lead: In Edmonds, hardwood on the main living level sells a house faster and photographs better, but new neutral carpet in the bedrooms, on the stairs and in a lower level is what buyers expect and the smarter pre-sale spend there.
blocks.detail: Buyers punish worn, stained or dated flooring far more than they reward any particular material. The winning formula is clean hardwood where people gather and fresh carpet where they sleep, done before the listing photos. Carpet labor runs $0.99 per sq ft, which is why the bedrooms are the cheapest lift in the house.

blocks.html: Edmonds sellers are often downsizing out of a 1960s Seaview or Perrinville rambler, and flooring is the first thing the listing agent mentions. The question we get at the showroom is blunt: do we pay for hardwood, or is new carpet enough? The answer depends on the room, on what is under the carpet, and on who is buying here: retirees who want move-in ready, and younger families who want hardwood but accept carpet upstairs.

blocks.text: What Edmonds buyers actually react to

items.title: Condition beats material
items.text: Agents tell us the same thing every year: clean, current flooring of any kind shows better than tired hardwood or matted carpet. A buyer who sees a pet stain deducts far more than the fix costs. Whatever you choose must look new in the photos.

items.title: Hardwood in the shared rooms
items.text: Living, dining, kitchen and entry are where buyers picture themselves. Hardwood there reads as quality and continuity, especially in the open remodels common in the Bowl. It is what competing listings will have.

items.title: Carpet upstairs is not a negative
items.text: Fresh, neutral carpet is what most Edmonds buyers still want upstairs: warmth, quiet, bare feet in February. Nobody walks away because the bedrooms are carpeted. They walk away because the carpet is beige from 1998.

items.title: Waterfront humidity shows in floors
items.text: Homes near the water carry more moisture year round, and inspectors look for cupped hardwood and musty carpet in lower levels. A dry lower level with new carpet reassures; damp anything scares.

blocks.text: Price your pre-sale carpet in Edmonds

blocks.html: Here is the trade in dollars. Carpet labor is $0.99 per sq ft over pad and $30 per step, 500 sq ft minimum, plus $0.45 per sq ft to pull and haul the old carpet and $0.25 to move furniture. Three bedrooms and a hall at 700 sq ft with a 14-step run is 700 × $0.99 + 14 × $30 = $1,113 in labor, plus $315 of tear-out, plus the carpet and pad, quoted at the estimate. Refinishing oak is $3.99 per sq ft all in, so a 900 sq ft living, dining and entry is $3,591. That is the choice Edmonds sellers are really making.

blocks.note: Labor only. The neutral carpet and its pad are quoted at the free estimate, and that is where a pre-sale budget is won or lost.

blocks.text: The Edmonds twist: check what is under the carpet

items.d: Lift a corner in a closet
items.text: Most 1950s to early 1970s Edmonds ramblers were built with oak strip flooring that got carpeted over in the 1980s. A closet corner tells you in two minutes whether you already own a hardwood floor.
items.note: Look for 2 1/4 in oak strips, often gray but intact.

items.text: Pet stains, water marks at the slider and tack-strip holes all sand out. Deep black urine stains and buckled boards may need patching.
items.note: We check thickness at a register to confirm it can be sanded.

items.text: If oak is under there, refinishing at $3.99 per sq ft is the highest-return move a seller can make, because the material is already paid for. New carpet then goes only where there is no wood.
items.note: Both rates are on the price list linked at the end.

items.text: Bedrooms often have the same oak. Refinished wood there is a bonus, not a requirement. Sellers on a budget refinish the shared rooms and carpet the bedrooms.
items.note: Continuity in the shared rooms, comfort in the private ones.

blocks.text: When new carpet is the better pre-sale spend

a.title: Choose it when
items: The room is a bedroom, stair run or lower level
There is no hardwood under the existing carpet

b.title: Choose it when
items: The room is the living, dining or entry level
Oak is already under the carpet and only needs refinishing
You have four to six weeks before photos
You plan to stay a few years and sell later

blocks.title: Do not carpet over hardwood to save time:
blocks.text: Sellers ask us for this every year as a quick refresh. Buyers' agents know to lift a corner, and hidden hardwood reads as a seller hiding something. Refinish the wood or leave the carpet honest; never bury a floor the buyer would have paid for.
Mistakes Edmonds sellers make with flooring

items.html: Choosing a trendy color. Cool gray looked current five years ago and now dates a listing. Warm greige photographs neutral and matches most paint.
Buying the thinnest carpet possible. Buyers walk on it in socks. A medium-density pad and a mid-grade nylon feel like quality without a premium price.
Replacing only the worst room. Three shades of beige in three bedrooms look worse than one worn carpet did, and the 500 sq ft minimum means doing them together usually costs no more labor.
Installing after the photos. Carpet is a one-day job; schedule it a week before the photographer, not the week after.
Ignoring the lower level smell. A musty basement needs a dehumidifier and a moisture-barrier pad, not just new carpet. See whether to replace carpet before selling.
Lift a closet corner in every carpeted room and note where there is hardwood.
Ask your agent which recent Edmonds sales you are competing with and what floors they showed.
Get one written quote covering both: refinishing the wood you have and carpeting the rooms that need it.
Keep the receipts and the carpet warranty for the buyer's packet. Our carpet installation page explains what a Wills quote includes.

faq.a: Worn, stained or dated carpet does. Fresh neutral carpet in bedrooms, on stairs or in a lower level does not, and many Edmonds downsizers prefer it there. At $0.99 per sq ft of labor it is also the cheapest way to make a listing look cared for. Carpet in living areas, kitchens or bathrooms is what hurts.

faq.q: Is it worth installing hardwood floors just to sell a house?
faq.a: On the main living level, usually yes, especially if oak is already under the carpet and only needs refinishing at $3.99 per sq ft. Installing new hardwood throughout a house you are about to leave rarely pays back in full; buyers reward the shared rooms and accept carpet in the bedrooms.

faq.q: Should I replace carpet or offer a flooring credit when selling?
faq.a: Replace it. A credit asks buyers to imagine the result and hire a contractor after closing, so most discount the offer heavily. New carpet is a one-day job that changes the photos and the showings immediately, and the labor is $0.99 per sq ft.

faq.q: What carpet color is best for resale?
faq.a: A warm neutral: greige, soft taupe or a light warm gray in a medium pile with a subtle texture. It photographs cleanly, matches most wall colors and hides footprints. Avoid stark white, cool blue-grays and anything patterned.

faq.q: Do buyers in Edmonds prefer carpet or hardwood in bedrooms?
faq.a: It is split, and it leans to carpet more than in Seattle. Retirees downsizing here like warmth and quiet underfoot; younger families like hardwood but rarely walk away over carpeted bedrooms. Fresh carpet upstairs and hardwood downstairs satisfies both.

faq.q: Can I put new carpet over the old hardwood to sell faster?
faq.a: You can, but you should not. Agents lift a corner, and hidden hardwood makes buyers wonder what else is covered. Refinishing wood you already own is nearly always the better return, and it is what the listing next door will have done.
